cita: Wang, Y., Yang, L., Chen, B., Zou, G., Xu, K., Tang, B., Xiong, F., Chen, S. y Li, Z. (2025). Text2Mem: A Unified Memory Operation Language for Memory Operating System.
problema: Existing LLM-agent memory frameworks (MemGPT, A-MEM, MemOS, mem0, Letta) expose only basic primitives (encode/retrieve/delete) with no formal, executable specification for higher-order controls (merge, promote/demote, split, lock, expire), leaving scope and lifecycle rules implicit and causing unpredictable, non-portable behavior across systems.
mecanismo: Text2Mem defines twelve mutually exclusive verbs across encode/storage/retrieval stages, each expressed as a typed JSON schema instance with a five-field backbone (stage/op/target/args/meta); a validator checks legality, a parser normalizes into typed operation objects, and adapters compile these into either a SQL-like reference backend or real memory-framework APIs (MemOS, mem0, Letta), unifying write/consolidate(merge)/forget(delete,expire)/update across representations.
evaluacion: Primarily a language/schema design paper: it does not run a live benchmark. It compares operation coverage against MemOS, mem0 and Letta qualitatively (Table I, native/partial/absent support matrix) and outlines 'Text2Mem Bench' as planned future work separating schema generation from backend execution, but reports no empirical results yet.
numeros_clave: Twelve verbs across 3 stages (1 encode, 9 storage, 2 retrieval), 5-field schema backbone, 3 frameworks compared in Table I support matrix (MemOS/mem0/Letta); no ablation/benchmark numbers reported (Text2Mem Bench is future work).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Text2Mem's typed 5-field schema (stage/op/target/args/meta, sec III-B) offers MF a formal vocabulary for narrative-memory operations that could type Tier-1 doc mutations beyond free prose.
The Update-verb example ('remember key points...becomes...dated action items') treats task/plan state as a memory object, but the paper never specializes a dedicated plan-state layer.
Merge/Split verbs (Table I) formalize consolidation-with-lineage as first-class operations that MF's promotion-of-gotchas mechanism could adopt directly.
Lock/Expire verbs attach audit trails and TTL/until governance (sec III-A.2.b), supporting MF's provenance/staleness concerns for Tier-1 docs.

notes: Table I (sec III-A.3) is the qualitative support matrix vs MemOS/mem0/Letta; Text2Mem Bench (empirical eval) is explicitly future work, not yet run.

cita: Deshpande et al. (2025). MEMTRACK: Evaluating Long-Term Memory and State Tracking in Multi-Platform Dynamic Agent Environments.
problema: Existing memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval) focus on single-thread conversational settings; there is no benchmark for long-term memory and state tracking in dynamic, multi-platform enterprise agent environments (Slack/Linear/Git) with noisy, conflicting, cross-referring information.
mecanismo: MEMTRACK is a benchmark harness, not a memory system: a dockerized environment with real Slack/Linear/Git servers injects a chronologically platform-interleaved event timeline; agents are queried with sequential (incl. follow-up) questions while memory tools (Mem0 vector store with ChromaDB, Zep knowledge-graph) or no memory are attached, and Correctness (LLM-judge), Efficiency (tool-call count), and Redundancy (subsumed tool calls) are measured.
evaluacion: GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro agents tested with NoMem/Mem0/Zep across 47 curated multi-platform instances (mean 39.9 events, mean 4.01K event tokens), results averaged across 5 runs, Correctness scored via an LLM-judge (GPT-4o).
numeros_clave: Table 3: GPT-5+NoMem Correctness=0.601 vs GPT-5+Mem0=0.610 vs GPT-5+Zep=0.601 -- memory components give NO significant lift; best model (GPT-5) only ~60% Correctness; Gemini-2.5-Pro ~0.14-0.144 (about 4x worse than GPT-5); Redundancy ~20.6-24.0%; Table 1: 47 instances, mean 39.9 events/instance, mean 4.01K event tokens, mean timeline span 878h.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 3 shows Mem0/Zep retrieval adds NO significant Correctness gain over NoMem (GPT-5: 0.601->0.610->0.601), a measured case where a vector/graph retrieval layer does not help -- cautions that MF's ADR-019 bet on measured retrieval only pays off with the right design, not any store.

The benchmark treats the Git/codebase as one of three memory-relevant platforms (sec 3) alongside Slack/Linear, evidencing that versioned code/docs are a first-class memory source, though MEMTRACK does not itself propose a docs-as-truth tier.

Sec 2 flags that forgetting/retention policy 'is understudied' (citing Shan et al.) and MEMTRACK's conflict-resolution questions test whether agents notice contradictory info (sec 3), but the benchmark itself does not measure negative-knowledge/re-derivation strategies.

Efficiency/Redundancy metrics (sec 4.2) explicitly penalize excess/duplicate tool calls (TC_min=10, ~20% redundancy measured, Table 3), confirming MF's context-economy concern that unmeasured retrieval wastes tokens.

notes: Table 3 (sec 5) has the Correctness/Efficiency/Redundancy numbers; Table 1 has dataset stats; the forgetting-understudied claim is sec 2 citing [41].

cita: Modi et al. (2025). Debugmate: an AI agent for efficient on-call debugging in complex production systems.
problema: On-call software engineers debugging complex, distributed production systems face heavy cognitive load navigating vast codebases plus org-specific context that LLMs are not pretrained on; prior debugging agents (SWE-Agent) or context-selection tools don't integrate internal docs/codebase/incident history with external knowledge.
mecanismo: DebugMate combines RAG (LangChain RetrievalQA plus OpenAI embeddings, query expansion, cross-encoder reranking) over internal docs/knowledge-base, a Neo4j dependency graph over microservices, Git-change ranking (an 'election' over batches of 20 changes), and Tree-of-Thought branching (a parent agent spawns child agents per code module, DFS ordered by confidence) atop ReAct, plus short/long-term memory that stores code dependencies and class hierarchies as intermediate steps fed back into the LLM.
evaluacion: Evaluated on (1) DebugBench logical-error benchmark vs GPT-4-0613, (2) Observe.AI's historical P0/P1 reliability incidents (longest 10% resolution time), and (3) 16 real-world bugs from 5 Java open-source repos (Elasticsearch, Kestra, Dubbo, OpenSearch, Jenkins); ablations remove stack trace, KB/DP search, or replace Tree-of-Thought with Chain-of-Thought.
numeros_clave: 82% DebugBench vs GPT-4-0613's 75%; 83% ObserveAI vs 58%; 71.4% open-source vs 42.8% (Table 2); +20% accuracy vs baseline per abstract; ToT-to-CoT ablation drops Err.Fixed from 83.33% to 50.00% and avg reviewed function calls from 6 to 3.4 (Table 1); 14/16 root causes found, correct/partial fixes in 11 of those, on 5 real OSS repos (sec 4.1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: DebugMate's KB/DP-Search ablation (Table 1) shows removing internal docs/KB access raises search depth to 7.56 but only reaches 71.43% Err.Identified vs 83.33% with full access -- internal documentation measurably drives root-cause accuracy, backing MF's docs-as-truth tier.

Table 1's controlled ablations (no stack trace, no KB/DP, CoT-vs-ToT) isolate which retrieval/reasoning components move Err.Identified/Err.Fixed, exemplifying the measured-retrieval-layer discipline (ADR-019) rather than assuming any RAG component helps.

The Code Search tool dynamically prompts the user to paste a reduced snippet when content exceeds the token limit (sec 2.1), a manual token-economy fallback rather than an automated compaction/caching strategy.

Long-term memory stores 'valuable information like code dependencies and class hierarchies' (sec 1) reused across debugging sessions, a concrete instance of promoting transient findings into a durable structural map, close to MF's gotcha-to-recipe consolidation.

notes: Table 1 (ablations: no-stack-trace, no-KB/DP, ToT->CoT) and Table 2 (DebugBench/ObserveAI/OpenSource accuracy) are the numeric anchors; sec 4.2 lists 3 concrete failure cases.

cita: Vaithilingam et al. (2025). Semantic Commit: Helping Users Update Intent Specifications for AI Memory at Scale.
problema: As AI systems accumulate 'intent specifications' (CLAUDE.md-like files, Cursor Rules, game design docs, ChatGPT memories), integrating new information at scale can silently conflict with prior entries; plain LLM whole-document regeneration or vanilla verbatim-store RAG cannot detect multi-hop semantic conflicts, and it is unclear what interface affordances help users update these documents with confidence.
mecanismo: SemanticCommit builds a knowledge-graph-based RAG pipeline (PageRank relevance over an induced KG) to retrieve candidate-conflicting chunks, classifies each as conflict/ambiguous/no-conflict (deliberately loosened toward recall over precision), then an LLM proposes edits (add/update/delete) that a human reviews locally (diff-style) or globally before committing -- decomposing retrieval from generation/classification, unlike InkSync's single-shot detect-and-resolve or DropAllDocs' whole-context classification.
evaluacion: Benchmarked kg-pagerank against DropAllDocs (all docs in context, no retrieval) and InkSync (single-shot detect+resolve) on 4 custom benchmarks (Labyrinth, Mars, FinMem, CursorRules; Table 1) with GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini, reporting accuracy/precision/recall/F1 (Fig. 5); plus a 12-participant within-subjects user study comparing SemanticCommit to ChatGPT Canvas on a Mars game-design doc and a financial-advice agent-memory task (3 sub-tasks each), measuring completion, NASA-TLX workload, and Likert preference.
numeros_clave: SemanticCommit's recall is 1.6x DropAllDocs and 2.2x InkSync; F1 ties DropAllDocs and beats InkSync by 1.6x; precision is 1.6x lower than DropAllDocs (Fig. 5); Table 1 benchmarks: Labyrinth 35 chunks/17 modifications, Mars 30/25, FinMem 30/17, CursorRules 65/19; user study N=12 participants, 2 tasks x 3 sub-tasks each.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper explicitly frames CLAUDE.md/Cursor-Rules-style intent specs as 'reviewable, comprehensible' documents that ground AI decisions (sec 2) -- the same docs-as-truth premise MF's Tier-1 rests on, with a concrete update-conflict problem MF's write-trigger (G-M1) will eventually hit.

The kg-pagerank retrieval stage (Fig. 5) measurably beats naive whole-context (DropAllDocs) and single-shot (InkSync) baselines on recall (1.6x/2.2x, sec 5.1.3), a concrete pattern MF could adopt for measured retrieval over docs.

SemanticCommit's conflict-detection UI (Fig. 1) is a human-in-the-loop staleness/consistency check before a doc mutation lands, a candidate mechanism for MF's provenance/staleness gate on Tier-1 writes.

Sec 2.1.1 notes intent specs 'encode dependencies among ideas' (sequential/heterarchical), i.e. cross-references between facts within ONE store -- related to but not the same as MF's multi-store-seams concern.

notes: Fig. 5 plus Table 1 (sec 5.1) hold the recall/precision/F1 numbers across 4 benchmarks; sec 6 has the 12-participant study design (Mars GDD + FinMem tasks, NASA-TLX).

cita: Wu et al. (2025). Git Context Controller: Manage the Context of Agents by Agentic Git.
problema: LLM agents doing long-horizon SWE/web-research tasks hit a context-management bottleneck: interaction histories grow unbounded, become costly to maintain, and are hard to reuse across sessions/agents; existing fixes (truncation, or Claude-Code/Gemini-CLI-style summarization into an agent.md) either discard fine-grained detail or make agents progressively worse as context is compressed.
mecanismo: Git-Context-Controller (GCC) reifies agent memory as a version-controlled file system under .GCC/ with a global roadmap (main.md) plus per-branch commit.md (milestone summaries), log.md (fine-grained Observation-Thought-Action trace) and metadata.yaml (structural/dependency metadata); agents call four operations -- COMMIT (checkpoint, regenerate a coarse summary, git-commit), BRANCH (isolated exploration state), MERGE (LLM-synthesized union of two branches' summaries/traces plus roadmap update), CONTEXT (windowed multi-resolution retrieval at global/branch/commit/log/metadata level) -- turning transient token streams into a navigable, git-like memory workspace.
evaluacion: Compared against ReAct, SWE-Agent, Summary-Agent ('summarize-when-full'), and Folding-Agent baselines across 6 LLM backbones (GPT-5, GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, GLM-4.5-Air, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Claude-4-Sonnet) on BrowseComp-Plus (N=150, Pass@1) and SWE-Bench Verified (N=500, Pass@1) in Table 1; also compared on SWE-Bench-Lite against 26 published systems (Table 2, percent resolved/cost/tokens).
numeros_clave: GCC+Claude-4-Sonnet: SWE-Bench Verified Pass@1=0.802 (state of the art, +6.2pp over Folding-Agent's 0.740); GCC+GPT-5 BrowseComp-Plus Pass@1=0.834 (+1.9pp vs Folding's 0.815); GCC+GPT-5 SWE-Bench Verified=0.790 (+4.5pp); GCC uses MORE tool calls (101.5 vs Folding's 95.3 on SWE-Bench); SWE-Bench-Lite: GCC 48.00% resolved vs AgentLess 46.00% (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: main.md is explicitly 'the canonical source of the project's overall intent' shared across branches (sec 2.1), a concrete typed-doc-as-truth pattern; commit.md/log.md/metadata.yaml stratify it by abstraction level, close to MF's Tier-1 vs derived-index split.

main.md stores 'high-level project goals, key milestones, and the to-do list' as first-class versioned state (sec 2.1), directly measuring that plan-state-as-memory contributes to SOTA task resolution (Table 1) -- strong external support for MF's PLAN-ESTADO bet.

COMMIT regenerates a coarse summary St from St-1 plus new work (sec 2.2) and MERGE runs an explicit synthesis operator over two branches' summaries -- a formal consolidation-with-lineage mechanism MF's gotcha-promotion could mirror.

GCC deliberately spends MORE tool calls than baselines (101.5 vs Folding's 95.3 on SWE-Bench, sec 4) to get better accuracy -- evidence that MF's context-economy goal (fewer tokens/calls) can trade off against task success, not a free win.

notes: Table 1 (sec 4, BrowseComp-Plus N=150 / SWE-Bench Verified N=500 Pass@1 by backbone) and Table 2 (SWE-Bench-Lite vs 26 systems) hold all the numbers; sec 3.2 fixes CONTEXT's commit-window K=1.

cita: Mohsenimofidi et al. (2025). Context Engineering for AI Agents in Open-Source Software.
problema: As coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex/AGENTS.md, Gemini CLI) become more autonomous, they need machine-readable 'AI context files' analogous to human README/docs to encode project conventions, architecture, and build/test commands -- but almost nothing empirical is known about whether and how OSS developers actually adopt, structure, or maintain these files in practice.
mecanismo: A mining-software-repositories study: from 10,000 curated GitHub repos (SEART filtering: non-fork, >=2 contributors, licensed, active, top-10 languages, popularity+maturity ranking) they scan for 4 context-file formats (Copilot instructions, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md), qualitatively code the 155 AGENTS.md files' section headings into 14 content categories (Table 1) and 5 writing styles (descriptive/prescriptive/prohibitive/explanatory/conditional), and manually classify commit-level changes into categories (Table 2, e.g. Add/Modify/Remove instruction(s)) to track how the files evolve.
evaluacion: Adoption measured across 10,000 GitHub repos (RQ1); content/structure via qualitative coding of 155 AGENTS.md files' headings (RQ2, two-author coding guide over 91 lemmatized headings); evolution via commit-history mining of the 10 files with >=10 commits, yielding 169 hand-annotated commits (RQ3, 37% of all collected commits).
numeros_clave: 466/10,000 repos (4.7%) had adopted an AI context file (RQ1); CLAUDE.md avg 287 lines (SD 112), Copilot-instructions avg 310 (SD 127), AGENTS.md avg 142 (SD 231, highest variance); of 155 AGENTS.md files, 77 (50%) never modified after creation, 36 (23%) modified once, 32 (21%) modified 2-7 times; 111/169 commits (66%) touch exactly one change category, top categories 'Add instruction(s)' (78) and 'Modify instruction(s)' (59) (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The empirical finding that AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files are 'versioned, reviewed, quality-assured' project artifacts (sec 5) that agents load into every prompt is direct field evidence for MF's Tier-1-docs-as-truth premise, at real OSS scale (10k repos).

Sec 4.1 finds (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) co-occur in 25 repos with no consolidation observed -- real projects already fork the SAME facts across multiple context-file formats, an instance of the multi-store-seam risk MF's COSTURAS anchor targets.

50% of AGENTS.md files (sec 4.3) are never updated after creation and changes mostly 'fine-tune instructions' rather than promote/demote content -- suggests real projects rarely practice active consolidation of their docs, a gap MF's CONSOLIDACION mechanism could fill.

Table 2's most frequent change categories ('Add instruction(s)' 78, 'Modify instruction(s)' 59) show write-triggers do occur in practice, but the paper explicitly defers WHY a change was made (intent) to future work, leaving the write-trigger question open.

notes: Table 1 (14 content categories) and Table 2 (9 change categories, 169 commits) are the core evidence tables; RQ1 adoption stat (466/10,000) is in sec 4.1.
